agent AGENTS.md api app bootstrap.sh CLAUDE.md docs package-lock.json package.json README.md scripts skills-lock.json team-setup tmp vercel.json # DelayedBahn — error404.ai Share your train trip, and delayedBahn tells you how late each train is likely to be and whether you will make your change. It learns from Deutsche Bahn's own timetable and delay data. Built by team error404.ai at the European Hackathon League Zurich. ![Demo](docs/images/demo.png) ## Contents 1. [Problem](#problem) 2. [What we built](#what-we-built) 3. [The app](#the-app) 4. [Data](#data) 5. [What the DB data solves](#what-the-db-data-solves) 6. [Architecture](#architecture) 7. [Model](#model) 8. [Approach: two methods, combined](#approach-two-methods-combined) 9. [Evaluation](#evaluation) 10. [Code structure](#code-structure) 11. [Quickstart](#quickstart) 12. [Team](#team) 13. [Built with](#built-with) 14. [Screenshots](#screenshots) --- ## Problem - Everyone who travels with Deutsche Bahn knows the situation: trains are late and connections break. - The DB app shows the planned journey, not the chance that it actually works. - We cannot fix delays for everyone. But we can give each of our travellers a more reliable and comfortable journey, and that is where the app comes in. ## What we built - **Share a trip** from the DB app into our web app. It reads the trains, stations and times. - **Get a forecast per train**: likely arrival delay, a range, and the chance of making each change. - **Get advice**: the plan is fine, add buffer, or take an earlier or later connection. ## The app - **Start screen:** paste the text you copied from the DB app, or share it straight from your phone. The app can be installed on your home screen. - **Map:** your route drawn on a map of Germany, with the trains moving along it. - **Train cards:** one card per train with the likely delay, the range, and a short explanation from the model. - **Advice:** a clear verdict for the whole trip, and other options if a change looks tight. --- ## Data ### Sources All product data comes from Deutsche Bahn's official API Marketplace. | API | What we use it for | Endpoints | Auth | |---|---|---|---| | [Timetables](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/timetables) | Planned stops, live delays, cancellations, platform changes, route of every train | `station/{name}`, `plan/{eva}/{date}/{hour}`, `fchg/{eva}` | `DB_CLIENT_ID`, `DB_API_KEY` | | [RIS::Stations](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/ris-stations) | Official station names and EVA numbers | `stop-places/by-key` | Same keys | - **Historic DB data:** stored responses from the same Timetables feeds, one row per train per stop, published as [`piebro/deutsche-bahn-data`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/piebro/deutsche-bahn-data). The model is trained on this. - **Live DB data:** fetched from the APIs when a traveller shares a trip (`scripts/db_live_extract.py`, `trip/live.py`). ### Agentic retrieval pipeline - **Search:** an agent looks for data sources that could help explain delays (`db_route/discover/`). - **Decide:** it proposes which sources and which columns to keep, and which to drop. Every decision is then checked by fixed rules in code. - **Clean:** noise and irrelevant data are filtered out, so the model gets clean input that can be explained. - **Combine:** historic DB data and live DB data end up in the same format for the model. ## What the DB data solves | Traveller problem | DB data that answers it | |---|---| | "Which train and station is this?" | Timetables `station` lookup and RIS::Stations turn names from the share text into exact station IDs | | "Is my train late right now?" | The Timetables change feed (`fchg`) gives the current delay at every stop the train has passed | | "Will it get worse before my stop?" | Planned route and stops ahead, plus how earlier trains on the same line did today | | "Is this station having a bad day?" | Late share across all trains at the station recently | | "Will this train be cancelled?" | Cancellation flags in the change feed, and how often this route was cancelled before | | "Will I make my change?" | Planned arrival and departure times of both trains, combined with both delay forecasts | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD A["Live DB data
today's delays from Timetables + RIS::Stations"] --> P["Agentic retrieval pipeline
keeps what helps, drops noise"] B["Historic DB data
past delays, every train, every stop"] --> P P --> C["Delay model
fine-tuned Llama 3.2"] C --> D["Web app
shared trip in, forecast out"] ``` 1. **Collect:** we read timetables and delays from the DB APIs. 2. **Clean:** the retrieval pipeline keeps the useful data and drops the noise. 3. **Learn:** the model learns how delays grow along a trip from historic records. 4. **Predict:** when you share a trip, the app sends it to the model together with today's live delays and shows you the forecast. ## Model - **Base model:** Llama 3.2, an open-source language model, fine-tuned on historic DB data with LoRA. - **Time series support:** built with [OpenTSLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02410), so the model can read time series next to text. - **Input:** for one train and one stop it is heading to, the delays so far on this trip, how earlier trains to that stop did, and the recent lateness of the station. - **Output:** the most likely delay in minutes, a range, and the chance of cancellation. - **Connections:** the chance of making a change comes from the two trains' forecasts and the planned transfer time (`trip/connection.py`). ## Approach: two methods, combined The model can take the same delay history in two ways (`--prompt-mode` in `trip/train.py`): - **Time-series embeddings:** the delay series go through a time-series encoder, which turns them into embeddings the language model reads directly. - **Pure text:** the same numbers are written into the prompt as text, together with a short sentence that describes them. - **Combined:** both at once, embeddings plus text. Each method is an existing tool on its own. The idea is to combine them. We train each one separately and then the combination, so the comparison shows what each part adds: text only, embeddings only, and embeddings plus text. ## Evaluation - **Baseline:** the model is compared against simple and statistical baselines built on the same information (`trip/baselines.py`). - **Split:** data is split by time. The model is tested on a later period it never saw during training, so no future information leaks into training. --- ## Code structure ``` api/ Vercel entry: sends /api/* to the backend app/backend/ Node API (no dependencies): parse share text, predict, recommend app/frontend/ React web app: paste or share a trip, forecast, advice, map app/agents/ Python: data pipeline, model training, model server src/features/db_delay/trip/ the delay model (build, train, serve) src/features/db_route/discover/ agentic retrieval pipeline src/features/db_route/ route-level delay experiments scripts/ DB Timetables and RIS::Stations clients team-setup/ team coordination: tasks, decisions, hooks bootstrap.sh local setup check ``` | File | What it does | |---|---| | `scripts/db_live_extract.py` | Calls Timetables and RIS::Stations, merges plan and changes into one row per train per stop | | `app/agents/src/features/db_route/discover/run.py` | Runs the retrieval pipeline: search, assess, probe sources | | `app/backend/src/features/share-parser/grammar.js` | Reads DB share text into a journey (`POST /api/journeys/parse`) | | `app/backend/src/features/delay-prediction/routes/delay-prediction.js` | Asks the model for each train, works out change risk (`POST /api/predict`) | | `app/backend/src/features/recommendation/routes/recommendation.js` | Gives the verdict and alternatives (`POST /api/recommend`) | | `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/build.py` | Turns stop records into training examples | | `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/train.py` | Fine-tunes the model in text, embedding or combined mode | | `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/serve.py` | Serves forecasts to the backend, using live Timetables data | --- ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/KiraKami-dev/temporal_ai_error404.ai.git cd temporal_ai_error404.ai cp .env.example .env # add DB_CLIENT_ID and DB_API_KEY from developers.deutschebahn.com ln -s ../../.env app/backend/.env python3 scripts/db_timetables.py "Hamburg Hbf" # live departures from DB cd app/backend && npm run dev # terminal 1: API on http://localhost:8000 npm --prefix app/frontend ci && npm --prefix app/frontend run dev # terminal 2, repo root: app on http://127.0.0.1:5173 ``` To run the trained model locally, see "Model files (required)" in `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/README.md`. ## Team error404.ai — Akshat Khair, Gaurav Kulkarni, Jonas (`josteng`), Yash (`yash-epte`) ## Built with - European Hackathon League Zurich - Deutsche Bahn API Marketplace: [Timetables](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/timetables), [RIS::Stations](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/ris-stations) - [OpenTSLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02410), Llama 3.2, Nebius GPUs --- ## ### Model files (required)

The checkpoint and the data around it are not in Git. Running the model locally needs three files:

| File | Size | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint.pt` | 102 MB | The shipped embedding model, split mode on the v7 data after 6,000 steps (long delay history, same-train gains and corridor series through the time-series encoder): bucket key `models/db-trip-delay-v7-split-6k.pt` (`nebius/sync_bucket.sh get`, S3 keys in the root `.env`), or `checkpoint.pt` in the team's `delayedBahn-model.zip`. The submitted text model, `models/db-trip-delay-final.pt`, runs with `PROMPT_MODE=text` |
| `september_v7_test.parquet` | 11 MB | Recorded September trips with the v7 features: the recorded journeys and the stored history of live forecasts; in the zip |
| `xgb/` (`quantile.json`, `late.json`, `cancel.json`, `features.json`) | 218 MB | The refitted statistical forecast the v7 prompt reads; in the zip, or refitted at setup from `examples_v7.parquet` (bucket key `data/examples_v7.parquet`) in about 3 minutes |

The zip also carries `INSTRUCTIONS.md` with these steps. The base model (Llama 3.2 3B) and the
OpenTSLM start checkpoint download from Hugging Face during setup, about 7 GB. Setup puts
everything into one folder, kept separate from the unpacked files because it copies the checkpoint:

```
<dir>/.venv/                        Python 3.12 environment (torch with MPS, OpenTSLM, xgboost)
<dir>/model/checkpoint.pt           the model
<dir>/data/september_test.parquet   the recorded trips
<dir>/xgb/                          the statistical forecast; without it there is no live data
```

```bash
# with the ready xgb/ folder from the zip
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <files>/checkpoint.pt <files>/september_v7_test.parquet
cp -R <files>/xgb <dir>/xgb
# or refit it from the training examples
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <files>/checkpoint.pt <files>/september_v7_test.parquet examples_v7.parquet
```

Live data also needs `DB_CLIENT_ID` and `DB_API_KEY` (DB API Marketplace, Timetables API, free
plan) in the repo root `.env`, passed as `ENV_FILE` to `start`.

### Live on a laptop (Apple silicon)

The 3B model fits an Apple silicon laptop: `run_local.sh` builds the environment, then serves a
checkpoint live on MPS and starts the team backend and PWA in front of it. Forecasts are computed
for any recorded September trip, not only for saved ones.

```bash
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> db-trip-delay-v7-split-6k.pt september_v7_test.parquet
trip/run_local.sh start <dir>    # model on :8502, app on http://localhost:8000
```

Checked: v7 text on MPS reproduces the H100's saved test forecasts (same median and 10 to 90%
range on the sampled trips, distributions within bf16 noise), loads in a few seconds and answers
a two-leg journey in about two seconds. For an unstacked checkpoint such as final-v2-text, pass
`DROP_XGB=1` at setup so its prompt has no XGBoost sentence.

### Live DB data

With the statistical forecast refitted once (`live_xgb.py`, same features and settings as
`baselines.py`; it reproduces the September `xgb_*` columns with correlation 0.999), `serve.py
--xgb` answers legs that have no recorded trip from the DB Timetables API (`live.py`, reusing the
client and plan/change merge of `scripts/db_live_extract.py`). The row follows `build.py` at
t0 = now:

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Run delays (origin and the 4 stops before boarding), previous trains at the target (6 h), corridor trains (3 h), the target's last 3 hours | Live: `plan` per station hour, `fchg` per station |
| 90-day history at the target, same train number's earlier days | Latest stored rows (September scrape) |
| Older station hours, nationwide hours | Stored, filled by hour of day |
| `xgb_*` | Refitted XGBoost-v7 on the assembled row |

A cold leg costs 15 to 40 calls (station lookups and plan hours cached for the process, change
feeds for a minute), so one key at 60 calls per minute serves about two new legs per minute. The
nationwide and multi-day inputs need a collector over all ~5,300 stations (about 3 keys at the
archive's cadence) or the public archive to become fully live.

```bash
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <checkpoint.pt> september_v7_test.parquet examples_v7.parquet
ENV_FILE=<repo root>/.env trip/run_local.sh start <dir>
```

Checked: a real two-leg journey planned for the next half hour through `POST /api/predict` on the
team backend, answered in 9 seconds with 22 API calls per leg and no fallback.

### When DB live data fails

No, that's not intended. The map only draws trains whose route it can place, and on your trip two of the three touch **Buchloe**, which has no coordinates.

**Why it happens**

1. **Buchloe isn't in the station tables.** Coordinates come only from hand-made lists: 48 stations in `app/frontend/src/lib/stations.json` and 58 in `app/backend/src/features/share-parser/fixtures/stations.json`. Buchloe is in neither. The backend's DB lookup (`stations.js`) still finds Buchloe, but it only returns the EVA number and name. I checked with the real keys: Zürich HB, Augsburg Hbf and Erlangen come back with lat/lon, and Buchloe comes back as `{"evaNumber":"8000057","name":"Buchloe"}` with none.
2. **The route-shape fallbacks don't work for it either.** The rail router and OSM matching need coordinates at both ends. The only other source is the online timetable service, v6.db.transport.rest, which returned HTTP 503 when I tried it.

The camera fit ignores them too, which leaves only Augsburg → Erlangen. That's also why picking "train 1 / 3" doesn't move the map: `flyToLeg` has no area to zoom to and does nothing.

The forecasts aren't affected: the model works with EVA numbers, not coordinates. Only the map is.

- **Proper fix:** when a station isn't in the table, have the backend fetch its coordinates from RIS::Stations. The team already uses that API and the keys are in `.env`. Any German station would then show up on the map.
- **Optional:** show a short note such as "1 train can't be drawn on the map" instead of hiding it silently.
